exposure: mode of first delivery (vaginal breech vs. breech CS)
outcome: composite maternal outcome (fourth-degree perineal injury, postpartum hemorrhage requiring blood transfusion, hysterectomy, death)
composite infant outcome (stillbirth, extremely preterm birth, moderate to severe hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy, therapeutic hypothermia, death)
cohort: The study included 23,062 women in Sweden who had a first singleton breech birth at >=34 gestational weeks between 2000-2019, followed by a subsequent singleton birth.
finding: Overall, the chance of a two-children family achieving severe adverse composite outcomes for either mother or infant was high and similar, regardless of the mode of the first breech birth.
mod_finding: The study found that the overall chance of a two-children family without severe adverse maternal or infant outcomes was similar between groups regardless of the first breech birth mode, although specific infant risks were higher for vaginal breech in the first birth and lower in the second birth.
